Red flags: 2023 refusal to circulate a fellows' open letter on Gaza
- At the end of October 2023 the Akademie's leadership received an anonymous email signed "fellows" with a link to an open letter whose signatories included current and former fellows, asking the leadership to spread it through the Akademie's channels; the letter was published on a private, anonymous Instagram account, and the ministry says its reach and the reactions to it were small (Baden-Württemberg Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts, reply in Landtag Drucksache 17/5894, issued 11 January 2024).
- The leadership met the current fellows who had signed and told them it would not circulate the letter because it was "einseitig von antiisraelischen Positionen geprägt" (one-sidedly shaped by anti-Israeli positions, translated) and repeated arguments also used in antisemitic discourse (Landtag Drucksache 17/5894).
- The ministry states that the Akademie published its statement of 30 October 2023 at the ministry's request, and that the leadership wrote the text and agreed it with the ministry (Landtag Drucksache 17/5894).
- On 28 November 2023 Stephen Brauer and other FDP/DVP members of the state parliament tabled a motion asking the government to report on the episode, including what the letter's content suggested about "möglicherweise antisemitische Grundhaltungen" (possibly antisemitic attitudes, translated) among the signatories (Landtag Drucksache 17/5894).
- The ministry's reply, signed by Minister Petra Olschowski, says the letter criticises Israeli policy in Gaza and uses vocabulary typical of Israel-related antisemitism; the signing fellows told the leadership they did not want their criticism understood as antisemitic and expressed grief for the Israeli victims of 7 October (Landtag Drucksache 17/5894).
- The ministry adds that any discrimination, including antisemitism, can lead to the immediate end of a fellowship, and that after the statement the Akademie held an internal workshop with outside experts on democracy education and antisemitism research (Landtag Drucksache 17/5894).

SOURCES
- https://www.landtag-bw.de/resource/blob/264734/1ab8a43920d3fc30fd2af8a6f60dd8b0/17_5894_D.pdf (state parliament document)
reason: Every point checked against the text of Drucksache 17/5894 (motion of 28.11.2023, issued 11.1.2024, reply signed by Olschowski). Quotation corrected word for word; added the ministry's own line on the letter's small reach and the 'antisemitic discourse' reason the leadership gave. This file is the full account that replaces the record's wider_context item marked 'Unverified' (German Wikipedia citing the Stuttgarter Zeitung); that item and its note that the letter 'was not found' should be removed when this is merged. The 30 October 2023 statement's content already in wider_context is not repeated.

Red flags: 2022 dispute over moving works to a planned ministry museum in Antigua
- In July 2022 the museum's director Rudy Cotton said the ministry's new administration planned a new museum in Antigua to gather the most important pieces of all the national museums, and that the museum had given about 26 pieces to it against his wishes (Prensa Libre, Marysabel Aldana, 29 July 2022).
- Cotton said he feared the museum would be closed for at least 10 to 15 years: "Las obras van para el museo de ellos y con eso buscan cerrar el Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida" (the works are going to their museum and with that they seek to close the Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida, translated) (Prensa Libre, 29 July 2022).

Red flags: 2023 director's complaint over building works and moving the collection
- On 7 September 2023 the museum's administration said in a statement that the Ministry of Culture and Sports and its Vice Ministry of Cultural and Natural Heritage had taken arbitrary actions against cultural heritage, including moving works of art to places without suitable conditions (Emisoras Unidas, 7 September 2023).
- Cotton said the ministry under Minister Felipe Amado Aguilar Marroquín was moving the collection to the Museo de Historia Natural without proper care: "Las mil 200 obras están siendo trasladas al Museo de Historia Natural" (the 1,200 works are being moved to the Museo de Historia Natural, translated) (Prensa Libre, Marysabel Aldana, 7 September 2023).
- Unverified: Cotton said the minister had harassed him and taken legal action against him, with three administrative records, two criminal complaints and a judicial complaint seeking his immediate dismissal, which Prensa Libre reported were still before the courts (Prensa Libre, 7 September 2023); Emisoras Unidas reported Cotton saying the complaints had been dismissed.
- The ministry called the accusations false and said they were Cotton's personal claims, not the museum's as an institution (Prensa Libre, 7 September 2023), and that the works followed the procedures the law sets for heritage buildings: "son falsas las acusaciones por parte del director del museo" (the accusations by the museum's director are false, translated) (Emisoras Unidas, 7 September 2023).

WIDER CONTEXT
- In September 2016 the organisers of Massimadi, a four-day LGBTQ film, art and performance festival in Port-au-Prince led by the group Kouraj, said it had been called off after numerous threats of violence and a prohibition by a government commissioner; FOKAL and other co-hosts had been threatened with arson and other attacks (Associated Press, via CBS News, 27 September 2016).
- Lorraine Mangones, FOKAL's executive director, said: "FOKAL has been receiving threats of outrageous violence" (Associated Press, 27 September 2016).
- The capital commissioner, Jean Danton Leger, confirmed he issued an order to block the festival, telling a local radio station it was in part to protect Haiti's "moral and social" values; he had received a complaint in the preceding days from Senator Jean Renel Senatus (Associated Press, 27 September 2016).

SOURCES
- https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/massimadi-lgbt-festival-canceled-in-haiti-amid-threats-to-organizers

CRITICISM IN ART MEDIA
1. Hyperallergic: Annette Lin, "How a Museum Wields Its Power in Crafting a National Identity" (2019)
URL: https://hyperallergic.com/how-a-museum-wields-its-power-in-crafting-a-national-identity/
- Behind a registration wall; only the introduction was read. The points below are from Nonprofit Quarterly's account of the piece (Eileen Cunniffe, "Can a Single Museum Speak for the Nation?", 1 October 2019).
- The permanent collection's emphasis on Maya artefacts gives visitors the impression that the Maya were "the only culture to ever occupy pre-colonial Honduras", though they occupied only "the western fringes of the modern state"; Lin writes that this "underscores the disconnect between an artistic construct of a country and the lived experience of the majority of its citizens."
- The museum largely fails to acknowledge current unrest in Honduras, and Lin asks: "What does this place have to do with how Hondurans see themselves?"
- Lin contrasts a painting in the temporary galleries of a woman trying to leave the country with her two children with "the elevator music version of Honduran society the permanent exhibitions presented."
